## Overview

<!--
At a high-level address what your proposal is and how it will address
the problem identified. Highlight any benefits to the R Community that
follow from solving the problem. This should be your most compelling
section.

Include concrete actions you will take and estimated timeline.
-->

I will improve Arity's analysis of package code, extend its metadata for
dependencies, and test these changes together in complete editing workflows.

## Detail

<!--
Go into more detail about the specifics of the project and how it delivers
against the problem.

Depending on project type the detail section should include:
-->

### Minimum Viable Product

<!--
What is the smallest thing you can build that delivers value to your users?
-->

Language-server reliability

:   I will improve Arity's handling of shared and inherited roxygen
    documentation. References, renaming, and call hierarchy will handle quoted
    function names consistently. Renaming will produce valid R syntax, including
    in infix calls, or Arity will refuse the operation.

Package knowledge for editor assistance

:   I will publish versioned indexes for at least 100 CRAN packages meeting the
    quality criteria below, including packages outside the existing bundle and
    dependencies in the evaluation workflows. The indexes will contain exported
    names, symbol kinds, recoverable arguments and defaults, and help. They will
    also record deprecated and defunct functions identified from explicit
    declarations, with replacements where available. Arity will use these
    indexes for completion, hover information, signature help, and linting
    without local package installation.

    I will document the schema, automate weekly updates, and add a prefetch command
    for downloading indexes in bulk. The editor and CLI will use the same cached
    metadata and work with downloads disabled. Network access will remain an
    explicit user choice. Each index will record the package version and how the
    metadata was extracted.

Validation and documentation

:   I will test complete editing workflows on ten packages with cross-file
    references, imports, shared documentation, and nonstandard evaluation. I
    will update the guides for editors and continuous integration (CI),
    explaining how to use Arity alongside other R tools.

### Architecture

<!--
What does the high-level architecture look like?
-->

Arity's metadata harvester already reads serialized R objects and
installed-package help without running R. Its binary parsing and Rd decoding
overlap with
[r-documentation-rs](https://github.com/eitsupi/r-documentation-rs). I will
coordinate with its maintainer on consolidating these readers in
r-documentation-rs, reducing duplication and making improvements available to
other R tools. Arity will continue to handle package discovery, export
resolution, metadata indexing, caching, and editor integration.

As of September 2026, Arity bundles export names for over 500 packages and has a
workflow to refresh them weekly. The remote client already supports downloads,
disk caching, and versioned indexes, but accepts only exported names. I will add
a pipeline to publish richer indexes, extend the client to supply signatures and
help, and make cached exports available to the CLI. Local indexes will take
precedence, and Arity will show the package version when it uses a remote index.

### Assumptions

<!--
What assumptions are you making that, if proven false, would invalidate the project?
-->

Static analysis cannot determine what every name refers to at runtime. Arity
will refuse uncertain rewrites and withhold deprecation diagnostics when
function resolution or status is uncertain. I will document unsupported cases.
The publishing pipeline will initially target current package releases. An
available index may describe a different version from a project's dependency.
When Arity cannot establish that the versions match, deprecation findings will
identify the indexed release and remain advisory, without causing the CLI to
fail.

I will record missing fields and failed extractions, and older metadata will
retain the version of the package it describes. Backfilling historical releases,
selecting indexes from project lockfiles, argument-specific deprecations, and
signatures that require running R are outside this project's scope.

### External Dependencies

<!--
What external dependencies does the project have (e.g. libraries, services, other projects, etc.)?
-->

For the pilot, I will extract metadata from unpacked [R-universe binary
packages](https://docs.r-universe.dev/install/binaries.html), falling back on
packages installed in CI when needed. I will check the complete export lists and
samples of signatures and help against the same package versions in R, and use
roxygen2 to check documentation behavior. The source packages and extracted data
will retain their version and license information.
